svg.title: A nursing student says, "The Rinne test was positive, so this client's hearing is normal." What is the nurse's best response?
svg.desc: This is the trap. A positive Rinne (AC > BC) happens in a normal ear and in sensorineural loss — both routes are reduced there, but air conduction is still the better of the two, so the ratio is preserved. Only conductive loss flips it to negative . Rinne alone never gives you the whole picture.

g.text: STUDY HUB / QUESTION MAP
Sensory Disorders - Eye & Ear
Read the situation
A nursing student says, "The Rinne test
was positive, so this client's hearing is
normal." What is the nurse's best
response?
What fits here
"A positive Rinne only means air
conduction beat bone conduction, and that
is also true in sensorineural loss."
Why it fits
This is the trap. A positive Rinne (AC >
BC) happens in a normal ear and in
sensorineural loss — both routes are
reduced there, but air conduction is still
the better of the two, so the ratio is
preserved. Only conductive loss flips it
to negative . Rinne alone never gives you
the whole picture.
